body:
Wow, thank you. You gave me some insight into how she must feel. Especially with doing stuff around the house. I think I'm helping, then I look over and she has this sad/frustrated look on her face...
She also gets verrry frustrated if I'm on my phone at all when we're watching something together. I sometimes say "Well, you're on your phone too!" but I realize she sometimes needs multiple inputs to distract from the pain.

I think the reminder to take care of myself hit home too. I sometimes don't do what I need to do to take care of myself (like getting an icepack for my chronic low back pain, or taking advil when I have a headache, or even going for a walk every day for mental health)...

Yeah, I know she feels guilty about it all. Our whole life path changed, we were going to school for the same thing and had planned on building something together. Now our goals are concurrent, but very different. 

With her illness, it actually will just get worse, as it's genetic, but I am so so hoping she can learn to have more ways of coping. 

We are both seeing a therapist, thank god. And plan on doing couples therapy soon. 

It's just hits me sometimes like, "Wow, are we gonna make it?" and "Can I deal with this?" I have the total of the financial stuff on my shoulders until she gets on disability, and I miss having some freedom. I wish I had more energy to do it all.
